convoLines.text: "Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Good. We're better with you here. I mean that."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Sanne. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
Found something. Follow it to the moot.
Said. At the moot. Let the fire decide what it means.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I asked Enrique about the pantry run — Enrique's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the old burn east of camp in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
Counted.
"Anyway — I should get going."
You don't answer. The quiet turns pointed.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They nod, already turning away.
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago. Good talking."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"I count meals, not days. Three meals since the rain. Two since the alarm. Days are for people with calendars. I have a stomach. Hm."
"Still on what day it is. You know?"
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Anyway, that's me."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"Oh." A long pause. "I didn't think it was anyone's. It's gone — I ate it days ago. I'm sorry."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I'm sorry — I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"Rest and clean water aren't cutting it. If this turns, I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. I need someone who knows what they're doing."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"The whole fire was arguing about Flashbulb Moth last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Ugly' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Wild Strawberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Wolfgang: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Sanne. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I should get back to it."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you're staying — you didn't expect to say it, but you said it. Still true?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
"Still on that personal stuff."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Wolfgang grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Brunhilde is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

sayTrace.returned: They spread their hands, smiling — the words are missing, but the meaning lands anyway.

lines: d7: 🕯️ Enrique Ali is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d7: What Enrique kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d7: Carlos picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.
d7: 📖 LEARNED: Patient Aim (Level 1). One shot. You don't take the shot unless it's the shot.
d7: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d7: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d7: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d7: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Enrique Ali, 7 days. The mantle passes to Carlos Power.
d7: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Carlos Power, 27 — a Dentist. Their hands know different work now: Iron Stomach.
d7: The fire knew Carlos — solid ground, earned at this fire.

d17: Fresh food keeps days, not weeks. Smoke it over a fire to make it last.
d17: Snow by morning. (1°C — Cold) The ground goes iron — forage thin, walking dear.
d17: Gladys Liu reads the sky: rain tomorrow, cold.
